messages:
maya: quick update — I landed the stage-queue-refactor branch locally. It separates the init-phase queuer from the streaming-phase queuer (no more one-big-queue).

sam: nice. any numbers?

maya: 10k sample run on A100: 95p end-to-end latency for short-prompts down ~48% when bursts hit, p50 about same. throughput slightly lower overall (~-7%) because we're triggering different kernels on rapid phase flips.

nora: can you clarify "init-phase"/"streaming-phase" mapping? is init the cold KV + prompt decode?

maya: yeah — init-phase = prompt token prefill (KV writes/warm), streaming-phase = autoregressive generation (KV reads, small decode batches). We renamed to avoid copying the repo jargon.

dirk: what's the kernel thrash you mentioned?

maya: when a request transitions from init->streaming within the same batch window, the runtime sometimes picks a large-matrix kernel (good for long seq) and then immediately switches to a small-matrix kernel for the emitter tokens. That kernel selection jitter costs ~2-3ms per switch, amplified across many micro-batches.

lee: interesting. did you try adding a phase-hint to the kernel selector? e.g., prefer stable kernel for N tokens after phase change?

maya: implemented soft sticky kernels: selector now has a phase-sticky TTL (configurable). With TTL=64 tokens the kernel thrash metric drops to near-zero, and end-to-end latency improved back to baseline while keeping burst tail gains.

sam: trade-offs? memory / kv behaviour?
maya: KV warm windows are the other part — we added a tiny grace window on the init queue so KV writes complete and the first few reads in streaming-phase don't miss. This increased median warmup latency by ~0.6ms but reduces read-miss penalty that used to spike 95p.

nora: do we have config knobs exposed for canary? want to try token_budget_target tweaks per-customer tier.
maya: yes, added a config block. sample: 
```json
{
  "queuer": {
    "init_queue_size": 64,
    "stream_queue_size": 128,
    "phase_sticky_ttl_tokens": 64,
    "token_budget_target": 48,
    "max_concurrent_batches": 8
  }
}
```

dirk: token_budget_target 48? why that value?

maya: empirically a sweet spot for latency SLOs with our current kernel mix. Lower targets reduce batch formation time but increase kernel-context switches; higher targets help batching but hurt tail latency for small prompts.

lee: we need metrics for: phase-tagged 95p latency, kernel-switch count, kv-miss-rate, and batch-formation delay. Can someone add them to the per-route dashboard?

sam: I'll wire phase tags into the tracing (adds a small field: phase=init/stream at enqueue). infra-bot will post canary deploy when ready.

infra-bot: deploy queued — snapshot: stage-queue-refactor @maya -> canary env across us-west-2, 3 machines. Triggered by sam at 1802500400.

maya: running the canary now. plan: 4 hours, synthetic bursts + replay traffic at 10% RPS. If 95p regresses >5% we rollback.

nora: also watch our quantization fallback path — we saw a rare regression where tiny batches hit a quantized kernel that was slower for certain seq lengths. add a guard to prefer non-quantized kernel when batch_size < 4 and seq_len > 256.

maya: good catch — patching selector to consider quant flag + phase-sticky.

sam: post-canary steps: if stable, we expose two knobs in Console: per-route token_budget_target and phase_sticky_ttl. Also add a gating experiment for Dedicated customers.

lee: one more: please add a short note in eng-runtime README about the queuer split and the reason for phase hints, with the perf graph links. saves us repeated triage.

maya: will do. attaching initial perf graphs here: https://internal.perf/graphs/1802500000-stage-refactor (synthetic + replay overlays).

sam: great — thanks everyone. follow-ups: nora on KV warm window analysis, dirk on kernel selector unit tests, lee on dashboard wiring.

nora: i'll start a small test to model different KV eviction delays and report back.

dirk: I'll add fuzz tests for kernel selection on rapid phase changes.

maya: thanks — will update thread with canary outcome. :rocket:
